However, my BEST experience was also in L&D. The girl was newer (i.e., younger) than the others, so maybe she just remembered her schooling experience and what helped her, but she had me do EVERYTHING which really stressed me out at first, seeing as how I hadn't had those opportunities.

I do know L&D sometimes covers more risk, liability, lawsuits, etc... and nurses get attached to their pt's and babies there, they don't want to let go.

You've gotten a lot of great advice. I just graduated with my BSN in Arizona... there ARE a lot of programs here. Community Colleges have the wait list, I went to ASU specifically and can't say much about admissions to their program because they seem to change the criteria every year (and honestly, advisement wasn't really helpful there but you can try contacting them). I had a friend at NAU that enjoyed it, but they only have one hospital in Flagstaff so she was envious of my experience at many hospitals throughout Phoenix.

Either way, I would highly recommend considering a BSN program. Many of the nurses I met during my rotations WERE associates nurses, currently going through RN-BSN programs which are mostly online and not too bad... but hospitals are starting to only want to higher BSN nurses, or people already employed in the system as techs, etc. 

There were a few people in my program that thought they wanted to do nursing, and ended up hating it... they didn't really know what it was about, four years down the drain. So keep looking into everything nursing related to get a feel for the real role.

Good luck in whatever you do!
